subject: community-medicine
title: Food Toxins: Neurolathyrism, BOAA, Aflatoxins and Epidemic Dropsy

steps.title: Cereals and pulses as dietary staples
steps.tx: Forming the backbone of vegetarian nutrition in India, **cereal and pulse staples** supply the bulk of daily caloric and protein requirements across rural and urban communities. Cereals such as wheat, rice, jowar and bajra provide seventy to eighty percent carbohydrates, eight to twelve percent protein, and essential B vitamins; pulses like chickpea, pigeon pea, green gram and black gram supply twenty to twenty-five percent high-protein building blocks.
steps.say: Cereals and pulses form the heart of the Indian diet. Grains supply bulk energy and carbohydrates, while lentils and grams provide concentrated plant proteins to build muscle.

left.title: Cereal grains (rice, wheat)
points: Rich in methionine, deficient in lysine

right.title: Legume pulses (dal, gram)
points: Rich in lysine, deficient in methionine

steps.title: Lathyrus sativus and neurolathyrism
steps.tx: During severe drought and monsoon crop failure, agricultural labourers consume excessive quantities of khesari dal (Lathyrus sativus), precipitating the crippling neurotoxic disease **endemic neurolathyrism paralysis**. Khesari dal is a hardy, drought-resistant pulse that survives when all other crops wither; when it constitutes more than thirty percent of daily caloric intake over two to six months, progressive spastic paraplegia develops in young adult men.
steps.say: When drought wipes out crops, farm laborers survive on hardy khesari dal. Eating this pulse as more than a third of the daily diet for three months causes permanent leg paralysis.

nodes.label: Severe drought and failure of traditional crops
Khesari dal exceeds 30% of daily diet for 2 to 6 mos
Excitotoxic injury to Betz cells and corticospinal tracts
Permanent spastic paraplegia of lower limbs

steps.title: BOAA excitotoxicity and motor neuron degeneration
steps.tx: The biochemical culprit responsible for neurolathyrism is **beta-oxalylaminoalanine neurotoxin** (BOAA), also known as beta-N-oxalyl-alpha,beta-diaminopropionic acid (ODAP). BOAA acts as a potent structural agonist at AMPA glutamate receptors in upper motor neurons of the motor cortex (Betz cells) and anterior horn cells, driving intracellular calcium overload, mitochondrial failure, oxidative stress, and selective irreversible axonal degeneration of the pyramidal corticospinal tracts.
steps.say: The neurotoxin BOAA overstimulates glutamate receptors in brain motor cells. Flooding the cells with calcium permanently destroys the pyramidal nerve tracts that control the legs.

rows: Excitotoxic calcium influx via receptor channels
Mitochondrial depolarization and free radical burst
Pyramidal tract axonal apoptosis in spinal cord
Permanent spasticity; sensory pathways completely spared

steps.title: Clinical stages of neurolathyrism
steps.tx: Neurolathyrism progresses through four distinct clinical stages based on mobility impairment, presenting as pure upper motor neuron paraparesis with hyperreflexia, extensor plantar responses, and ankle clonus, sparing sensation and bladder control. The **stages of neurolathyrism** begin with latent and no-stick stages (stiffness, scissoring gait), advancing to the one-stick stage, the two-stick stage, and culminating in the crawler stage where the patient crawls on hands and knees.
steps.say: Neurolathyrism begins with stiff, jerky legs, progresses to needing one and then two walking sticks, and ends with the patient crawling on hands and knees. Sensation remains perfectly normal.

rows: Walks without aid; short jerky steps
Scissoring gait, crossed knees, walks on toes
Requires single walking stick for balance

Requires two crutches / sticks to walk

steps.title: Detoxification methods for khesari dal
steps.tx: Because BOAA is highly water-soluble and heat-labile, public health specialists promote practical **khesari dal detoxification techniques** before cooking. Steeping seeds in boiling water for thirty minutes and discarding the drained soak water removes roughly seventy to eighty percent of the toxin; parboiling seeds at processing mills or breeding low-toxin genetically selected cultivars (such as Mahateora) eliminates neurolathyrism risk entirely.
steps.say: Boiling khesari dal in water for thirty minutes and pouring away the cooking water removes eighty percent of the toxin. Modern agriculture also breeds low-toxin seed varieties.

nodes.label: Steeping khesari dal seeds in boiling water for 30 min
Sun-drying seeds prior to standard cooking
70 to 80% extraction of water-soluble BOAA toxin

steps.title: Aflatoxins: Aspergillus flavus and hepatocarcinogenesis
steps.tx: Improper post-harvest storage of groundnuts (peanuts), maize and parboiled rice in hot, humid conditions permits contamination by **Aspergillus flavus aflatoxin production**. The fungus elaborates four major mycotoxins (B1, B2, G1 and G2), with aflatoxin B1 being the most potent natural hepatocarcinogen known; hepatic cytochrome P450 metabolises it into an epoxide that forms covalent DNA adducts, inducing specific transversion mutations in the p53 tumour suppressor gene.
steps.say: Mould growing on damp groundnuts and corn produces aflatoxin B1, a powerful liver carcinogen. The toxin mutates the p53 gene, multiplying liver cancer risk, especially in hepatitis B carriers.

left.title: Acute aflatoxicosis
points: Acute hepatic necrosis, jaundice, high mortality
Reported in western India famine outbreaks

right.title: Chronic aflatoxin exposure
points: Low-level daily dietary intake in groundnuts
Synergizes with Hepatitis B to cause liver cancer

steps.title: Aflatoxin prevention and permissible limits
steps.tx: Preventing aflatoxin contamination requires rigorous **agricultural post-harvest drying**, reducing crop moisture content below ten percent within forty-eight hours of harvesting to halt fungal mycelial proliferation. Statutory regulations set an absolute upper permissible limit of fifteen to thirty parts per billion (ppb) for total aflatoxins in commercial groundnut kernels, mandating visual sorting to discard discoloured, shrivelled or mould-damaged nuts.
steps.say: Drying harvested peanuts below ten percent moisture stops mould from growing. Food laws strictly cap total aflatoxins at thirty parts per billion, requiring sorting to remove mouldy nuts.

rows: Raised dry wooden pallets in ventilated silos
Electronic or hand-picking of shrivelled kernels

steps.title: Epidemic dropsy: argemone seeds in mustard oil
steps.tx: When mustard seeds are accidentally or fraudulently contaminated with Mexican prickly poppy seeds (Argemone mexicana), consuming the pressed oil triggers explosive outbreaks of **epidemic dropsy intoxication**. Argemone seeds closely resemble mustard seeds in size, shape and colour, but possess a characteristic rough, pitted surface with a tiny pointed caruncle, making adulteration difficult for consumers to detect without chemical testing.
steps.say: Epidemic dropsy occurs when wild prickly poppy seeds are pressed into mustard cooking oil. The weed seeds look almost identical to black mustard seeds, making adulteration difficult to spot.

left.title: Genuine mustard seed (Brassica)
points: Yellow inside when crushed; clean pungent aroma
Completely safe culinary vegetable oil source

right.title: Argemone mexicana seed (Weed)
points: Rough, pitted, reticulated surface with pointed tip
White inside when crushed; odorless bitter taste
Releases lethal sanguinarine alkaloid into pressed oil

steps.title: Sanguinarine toxicity: capillary dilatation and glaucoma
steps.tx: The active toxic alkaloids sanguinarine and dihydrosanguinarine inhibit sodium-potassium ATPase and pyruvate kinase, causing widespread **generalized capillary dilatation and hyperpermeability**. Patients present with bilateral pitting pedal dropsy, gastrointestinal nausea, intense cutaneous erythema, tachycardia, high-output congestive cardiac failure, and bilateral ocular open-angle glaucoma with visual loss from elevated intraocular pressure, requiring immediate cessation of adulterated oil.
steps.say: Sanguinarine paralyzes blood vessel walls, causing widespread capillary leakage. Patients develop severe foot swelling, racing heartbeats, heart failure and blinding glaucoma.

nodes.label: Inhibition of Na+/K+ ATPase and pyruvate kinase
Widespread capillary dilatation and massive leakage
Bilateral pedal dropsy, heart failure, ocular glaucoma
